source.publisher: Londonderry Sentinel (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: returned unopposed: 'There will be no contest in the Coleraine Rural District. Two candidates - Messrs. W. J. Anderson ... and Matthew Workman ... - were nominated on Tuesday for Aghadowey electoral division, but yesterday afternoon Mr. Workman's nomination paper was declared to be invalid on the grounds that his proposer was not a Local Government elector' (Londonderry Sentinel 19 May 1949 p6, image OCR read).

note: Triennial election of the 21 electoral divisions of Coleraine rural district, one member each, polled on 2 June 1949. The Irish News prints the full nomination list of 18 May. Twenty members were nominated unopposed and Aghadowey had two nominations, but Workman's was declared invalid, so there was no poll. Aghadowey was not polled after all: Matthew Workman's nomination was declared invalid, leaving W. J. Anderson returned unopposed (Londonderry Sentinel, 19 May 1949, p. 6); Somerset, with no nomination, returned its retiring member John Henry as deemed re-elected (round-2 gap-fill, 7 Nov 2026). The outgoing member, T. J. Linton, did not seek re-election. Anderson is again returned for Aghadowey in 1958 (Londonderry Standard, 21 May 1958, p. 3). Returned unopposed.
